episodes.title: How a CPU Turns 1s and 0s Into Everything You See
episodes.description:
How do CPUs actually work? Design PCB's with Altium:  http://altium.com/yt/engineeringmindset
How does a CPU use billions of microscopic transistors to perform calculations and run software? In this video, we work from individual MOSFETs through logic gates, binary arithmetic and full adders to the ALU and CPU core.
See how processors fetch and execute instructions, how registers and L1, L2 and L3 cache work, how data moves between the CPU, RAM and storage, and why modern CPUs use multiple cores.

We also compare CPUs and GPUs, explain why GPUs contain billions of transistors, and show why their parallel architecture is so effective for graphics and AI.
Topics include transistors, MOSFETs, logic gates, binary, CPU architecture, ALU, registers, cache, RAM, GPUs and AI.

episodes.title: Why RCDs Fail: The Hidden Danger in Your Consumer Unit
episodes.description:
How RCDs and GFCIs prevent electric shock. Many people think a standard circuit breaker (MCB) protects them, but it only protects wiring. In this video we explain RCD / GFCI protection, how they work, and when they fail.
🎁FLUKE 1674 FC - https://amzn.to/40S50vi
👉 FLUKE 1674 FC Specification - https://tinyurl.com/Fluke-1674FC

WHAT WE COVER IN THIS VIDEO:
⚡ MCB vs RCD -- Why a standard circuit breaker only protects your wires, while you can still get a lethal shock.
⚡ THE PHYSICS OF A TRIP -- How a toroidal transformer and magnetic flux detect tiny current imbalances (leakage) in milliseconds.
⚡ GLOBAL STANDARDS -- The difference between RCCB, RCBO, and GFCI (North America vs. UK vs. Europe).
⚡ THE "BLINDED" RCD -- Why modern LED chargers and EV chargers can cause Type AC RCDs to fail (Saturation).
⚡ LIVE BENCH TESTING -- We use a Fluke Multifunction Tester and an Oscilloscope to see the trip waveform in real-time.

episodes.title: The Strange Discovery That Made Computers Possible
episodes.description:
How Edison's abandoned discovery started electronics To learn for free on Brilliant 👉  http://brilliant.org/Theengineeringmindset Brilliant’s also given our viewers 20% off an annual Premium subscription, which gives you unlimited daily access to everything on Brilliant.

Discover how Thomas Edison’s forgotten discovery sparked the creation of the vacuum diode, triode, and ultimately the transistor, the foundation of all modern electronics and the computer age.
In this video, we explore the evolution of diodes, semiconductors, LEDs, rectifiers, and the atomic science behind PN junctions, showing how a simple effect inside a light bulb transformed into a multi-trillion-dollar industry.

If you want to understand electronics, radio, silicon, germanium diodes, Zener diodes, Schottky diodes, LED technology, and the origins of modern computing, this is the perfect deep-dive.

Learn how to use a clamp meter to measure current safely. Stop struggling with multimeters for high current testing.

Clamp meters are essential tools for anyone working with electrical circuits who needs to measure current without breaking the connection. Unlike standard multimeters, a clamp meter allows you to handle much larger currents safely by sensing the electromagnetic field around a wire. This guide explains the practical differences between these devices and why a clamp meter is the safer choice for high-amperage tasks.

We break down the science behind how clamp meters work, specifically looking at the electromagnetic field of a wire. You will see the fundamental difference between testing alternating current circuits and DC circuits. We also touch on the differences between digital and analog models to help you choose the right equipment for your workbench. If you want to master your measurement techniques, grab the PDF guide linked below.
